providers.market_view: The US equity market enters the shortened Thanksgiving holiday week facing a period of reduced liquidity and technical fragility. Increased intraday volatility is expected as investors digest a heavy schedule of economic data, including PCE inflation and GDP revisions, alongside significant Treasury issuance. While recent AI-related volatility has subsided following leadership reinstatements, a 'liquidity squeeze' remains a primary risk factor. In this environment, market participants are shifting focus from momentum-chasing toward stocks with confirmed idiosyncratic earnings catalysts that show institutional support despite the broader macro-uncertainty.

# Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF) Has Investors Rushing Back.
...
Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (NYSE:ANF) is one of the 10 Stocks With Easy Double-Digit Gains.

Abercrombie & Fitch extended gains to a third straight day on Tuesday, surging 19.8 percent to end at $168.26 apiece after beating its earnings expectations and posting double-digit sales in the third quarter of fiscal year 2026.

In an updated report, the retailer giant said that it grew its attributable net income by 24 percent to $415.2 million from $334.8 million in the same period last year. Earnings per share were at $3.82, beating its earlier expectations of $2.90 to $3.20.

Net sales increased by 5.55 percent to $3.8 billion from $3.6 billion year-on-year, falling within its projected growth range of 5 to 6 percent.

# Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF) Stock Soars 23% After Delivering 16th Consecutive Quarter of Growth
...
Abercrombie & Fitch ANF +22.50% ▲ is up by 23% after the American apparel retailer reported its third-quarter fiscal 2026 results. For the three months ended October 31, Abercrombie posted revenue growth of 11% to $1.4 billion, marking the 16th consecutive quarter of growth and topping the estimate of $1.37 billion. Its adjusted EPS of $3.82 was also above the estimate of $3.09.

“We remain on track for another year of record net sales, strong double-digit operating margins and growth in earnings per share,” said CEO Fran Horowitz.

## Abercrombie Raises Full-Year Guidance

All geographic and brand family segments grew, with Abercrombie and Hollister revenue rising by 12% and 11%, respective
